content: Remark 2.2. We have used the version of the vector representation  \( V_{q_{1}}^{*} \)  that is dual to the representation conventionally used in the literature (see e.g. [4, 5]). In our convention this means that the operator  \( R(x|v) \)  acts on a wavefunction that corresponds to a diagram sitting above the crossing in the picture.

Using Theorem 2.1 it is easy to find the \(R\)-matrix acting on \((\mathcal{V}_{q_1}^*)^{\otimes N} \otimes \mathcal{F}_{q_2, q_3}^{(1,0)}(v)\): it is given by the composition of \(N\) \(R\)-matrices (2.1) along the horizontal line. The result is a difference operator in \(x_i\) \(i = 1, \ldots, N\) which is also a vertex operator acting on \(\mathcal{F}_{q_2, q_3}^{(1,0)}(v)\).

where  \( x_{i} \)  is understood as the variable on which the functions in the i-th  \( V_{q_{1}}^{*} \)  tensor factor depend. We call  \( \mathcal{O}(\vec{x}|v) \)  the transfer matrix.
Definition 2.4. Trigonometric Ruijsenaars-Schneider Hamiltonians \( ^{1} \) are the following difference operators

\[
H_{k}^{\mathrm{tRS},(N)}(\vec{x},q_{1},q_{2}) = q_{2}^{-\frac{k(k - 1)}{2}}\sum_{\substack{I\subseteq \{1,\ldots ,N\} \\ |I| = k}}\prod_{i\in I}\prod_{j\not\in I}\frac{q_{2}^{-1}x_{i} - x_{j}}{x_{i} - x_{j}}\prod_{i\in I}q_{1}^{x_{i}\partial_{x_{i}}},\qquad k = 0,\ldots ,N.\qquad (2.4)
\]
Trigonometric RS Hamiltonians commute [3] and their common polynomial eigenfunctions are given by Macdonald symmetric polynomials \( P_{\lambda}(\vec{x}) \):

where \( u_{i} = q_{1}^{\lambda_{i}}q_{2}^{i - N} \) for \( i = 1,\dots ,N \), \( e_k \) are elementary symmetric functions and \( \lambda = (\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots ,\lambda_N) \) is a partition (Young diagram). In what follows we will mostly be interested in the eigenfunctions for generic parameters \( u_{i} \); these are non-polynomial.
